title: Lior and the Group Chat
premise: Gideon Amberdale, a debate champion whose eloquence fails at home, has perfected the art of invisibility at Marsh Hollow High, counting down to graduation. When their best friend Priya vanishes, leaving only her car keys on the school steps, Gideon discovers she'd been investigating an anonymous group chat that doxxed and destroyed students—run by someone they both trusted. As Gideon digs through Priya's hidden evidence, they realize staying silent made them complicit, and exposing the truth may cost them the friendship's last fragile threads. In the end, Gideon finds Priya alive but changed, testifies before the school board with the truth no one wanted, and learns that loyalty without honesty was never loyalty at all.
about_author: Ines Marchetti is a former high school debate coach who spent six years watching teenagers say true things in competition and false things everywhere else. She writes from a small apartment above a laundromat, where she claims the dryers provide better rhythm than any metronome.

chapters.title: Forty-Seven Days
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Opening on a winning debate round Gideon doesn't care about, then a cold dinner scene showing the argument they can't win at home. Establishes the countdown calendar and the invisibility strategy. Emotional beat: numb competence masking dread.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Steps
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Priya doesn't show for their morning ritual; her keys sit neatly on the school steps, fob still warm. The school shrugs; her parents assume a runaway. Gideon notices her locker combination scratched out. Emotional beat: the first crack of real fear beneath routine.

chapters.title: What Best Friends Don't Say
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, flashing between the search and memories of three months of Priya's growing distance—missed lunches, a locked phone, a bruise she called 'nothing.' Gideon realizes they noticed everything and asked nothing. Emotional beat: guilt arriving ahead of answers.

chapters.title: Marsh Hollow Anonymous
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A classmate, Theo, shows Gideon screenshots of the group chat: rumors, outed secrets, a girl named Cass who transferred after being targeted. Priya's name appears in the chat's crosshairs days before she vanished. Emotional beat: the school's friendly surface curdling.

chapters.title: Everyone Was in the Chat
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon maps the chat's membership and finds half the senior class—including friends, teachers' kids, even Gideon themselves, added without consent. Deniability by design. Emotional beat: complicity as contagion; no one is clean.

chapters.title: Priya's Second Phone
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Following Priya's habits, Gideon finds a burner taped under the bleachers with photos, admin logs, and one contact saved only as 'MOD.' The chat has a moderator who curated cruelty like content. Emotional beat: purpose replacing paralysis.

chapters.title: Home Is a Losing Format
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon tries to tell their parents about Priya and gets lectured about priorities instead—the recurring argument where truth loses to appearances. Gideon stops trying mid-sentence. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened by contrast with the search's urgency.

chapters.title: Cass Comes Back
chapters.summary: Cass's POV (first shift). The transferred student returns unannounced, drawn back by news of Priya's disappearance. She recognizes the MOD's rhetorical fingerprints—phrases lifted straight from debate camp. Emotional beat: a survivor returning to the scene with receipts.

chapters.title: Debate Camp, Two Summers Ago
chapters.summary: Alternating Gideon/Cass POV. Flashback chapter: the summer intensive where Priya, Gideon, and a magnetic older mentor, Rowan Voss, bonded—and where the chat's language was born. Emotional beat: nostalgia turning sinister in retrospect.

chapters.title: The MOD Has a Face
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Cross-referencing timestamps, Gideon confirms Rowan—now a beloved teaching assistant—is the moderator. Confronting them privately, Gideon meets charm, deflection, and a quiet threat about college recommendations. Emotional beat: power wearing a mentor's smile.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Cage
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Other students beg Gideon to stay quiet: exposure means college rescissions, ruined reputations, Cass blamed as a grudge-holder. Gideon weighs silence as protection versus silence as surrender. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—loyalty vs. truth.

chapters.title: The Burner Rings
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At 2 a.m., Priya's burner receives a message from MOD: 'You were warned.' Then, impossibly, a second message: 'It wasn't me. I'm close. Trust no one at school.' Priya is alive—and watching. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Two Moderators
chapters.summary: Gideon and Cass's POV. They discover the chat had two admins: Rowan ran it, but someone inside the friend group fed him material. The betrayal is closer than Gideon can bear to look. Emotional beat: paranoia fracturing every remaining trust.

chapters.title: Theo Knows Something
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Theo's behavior unravels—deleted messages, a new phone, panic when Cass mentions timestamps. He confesses he leaked Priya's secrets to Rowan out of jealousy over a scholarship, believing it would be 'just talk.' Emotional beat: banality of betrayal.

chapters.title: Where Priya Went
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Interlude revealing Priya's flight: after Rowan threatened to release her family's immigration documents, she went dark to trace his leverage trail alone, staying with Cass's estranged aunt two towns over. Emotional beat: fear transformed into strategy.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Gideon and Priya's POV converging. Priya directs Gideon to Rowan's off-campus storage unit: printed dossiers on dozens of students, including Gideon—a file proving he always knew and stayed invisible. Emotional beat: shame as the final lock on the door.

chapters.title: Rowan Makes His Offer
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Rowan corners Gideon with a deal: hand over the archive copies, and he'll frame Theo alone, protect everyone's futures, write Gideon a glowing recommendation. It's a good deal. That's what makes it monstrous. Emotional beat: temptation articulated perfectly—the debate Gideon finally understands.

chapters.title: The Rebuttal
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon refuses—not with anger but with the debate training Rowan himself gave them, dismantling his logic point by point in front of witnesses. Rowan's mask slips; he threatens them openly. Emotional beat: the home-trained voice finally winning an argument that matters.

chapters.title: Board of Education
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Gideon, Priya, and Cass present the archive to the school board as parents shout and lawyers circle. Rowan denies everything until the admin logs surface. Emotional beat: justice outside the law—messy, public, insufficient, but real.

chapters.title: Consequences
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Fallout lands unevenly: Rowan arrested, Theo suspended and shunned, classmates who laughed in the chat facing nothing at all. Priya returns to school and won't sit with Gideon—her secret was exposed too, by Gideon's evidence. Emotional beat: victory that costs exactly what the blurb promised.

chapters.title: The Argument at Home
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Armed with everything learned, Gideon finally wins—or rather, ends—the recurring argument at home, telling their parents the whole truth without flinching. It doesn't fix them, but it changes the terms. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won selfhood.

chapters.title: Day One
chapters.summary: Gideon and Priya's POV, alternating short sections. Graduation day. Priya approaches Gideon at the steps where the keys were found; forgiveness isn't offered, but a beginning is. Gideon crosses the stage visible, counted, counted-on. Emotional beat: memory kept honestly, loyalty rebuilt on truth.
